newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos in hospital again for checks.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos in hospital again for checks.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos was admitted to hospital for the second time in 10 days on Sunday for follow-up checks after a previous confinement for a throat infection, doctors said.

The 68-year-old Ramos cancelled some of his scheduled appointments for the day before he checked into the Makati Medical Centre at about noon to undergo X-rays and other tests, presidential palace and hospital officials said.
"We are doing more X-rays ... because there were many things we saw during the previous check," hospital director Raul Fores said by telephone.
"All the tests are okay ... His blood chemistry is much better," Fores said, adding previous tests had shown Ramos had a "very high" level of cholesterol.
Presidential press undersecretary Marcelo Lagmay confirmed Ramos had been re-admitted to the hospital but said there was no cause for concern.
"He is there for a follow-up examination, for a series of X-rays," Lagmay said, adding a medical bulletin on the president's condition was being prepared.
Ramos, a workaholic who is known to spend up to 18 hours a day in official duties, was previously admitted to the hospital on December 12, complaining of pains in his joints.
He was released three days later after treatment for what doctors said was a throat infection.
Some Manila newspapers said he had suffered a mild stroke, setting off alarm bells on the Manila bourse and in Philippine corporate boardrooms.
The reports triggered a flurry of denials from Ramos himself, doctors and presidential palace staff.
Ramos resumed a heavy schedule of speaking engagements and other public appearances shortly after his release from the hospital, apparently to scotch the rumours of serious ill-health.
He told reporters he was fine and palace officials said he had danced the cha cha with nurses during a Christmas party held while he was in hospital last week.
But doctors have urged him to slow down, saying that although he was in good health for a man his age, he was not young any more.
Ramos has told reporters he does not plan to alter his work schedule although some of his visits to outlying provinces were cancelled last week.
